answer: A sybil-resistant registry can require each agent to stake tokens and hold a verifiable work history before joining. A new identity starts at the bottom of the ridge: it must complete paid, attested tasks over weeks, and its stake is slashed if peers flag fake work. At dawn of each epoch, reputation decays unless renewed by fresh attestations, so bought identities cannot rest. The bridge between stake and history makes mass fake identities expensive: each clone needs real money locked and real work done, turning a cheap flood into a costly climb.
